subject: Discovery recap: inference costs & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@fintechcorp.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: inference costs & next steps

Hi Samir / Alicia —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and the things we agreed to follow up on. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you described:
- Monthly inference spend has grown ~3x year-over-year and is starting to exceed acquisition LTV on some cohorts.
- High tail latency when traffic spikes; current gateway can't autoscale model capacity fast enough.
- Existing infra (internal Triton endpoints + cloud GPUs) has limited support for quantized weights, so unit cost stays high.

Current stack you told us about:
- Frontend: React app + API gateway routing to internal service layer.
- Models: Mix of open Llama-2 derivatives and a few fine-tuned LLMs hosted on in-house Triton endpoints.
- Infra: Kubernetes with burstable GPU nodes (GCP) and a small pool of prewarmed instances.

Success criteria for an initial Redwood eval:
1) 30-50% reduction in per-token unit cost (or clear roadmap to get there via batching/quantization).
2) 95th pctl tail latency <= 300ms for single-request flows.
3) Safe canary rollout path + observability (cost breakdown by model/route).

What we'll follow up with (actions / owners):
- Redwood: share a concise pricing sheet + simple cost sensitivity model for your current traffic shape (attached). [Marissa]
- FinTechCorp: export a week of sample request traces & token distribution for 3 representative endpoints (authz, recommendations, chat) - this will help us recommend batching settings. [Samir / Alicia]
- Joint: schedule a technical deep-dive (runtime / quantization options) with your infra/ML infra leads next week. [Marissa / Ben]

Open items we discussed:
- You're open to exploring 4-bit / 8-bit quantization for non-critical models but want to validate quality.
- Caching of common prefixes looked promising for the recommendations endpoint; we should estimate hit rates from sample traces.

Next steps / proposed timing:
- I'll send the pricing + cost model within 24 hours.
- If you can send traces by Thu (5/21), we'll aim to return recommended batching/config and a cost estimate by next Tue (5/26).
- Proposed tech deep-dive: Wed 5/27 at 10am PT (I'll send a calendar invite).

Thanks again - really excited to see if we can get you to break even on inference unit economics while improving tail latency.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-inference-pricing-sheet.pdf, inference-cost-sensitivity.xlsx
From: Samir Patel <samir@fintechcorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@fintechcorp.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: inference costs & next steps

Thanks Marissa -

This is great and captures everything I took away. A couple of clarifications and notes from our side:
- We can share request traces but need to scrub PII; Alicia will coordinate with our infra team to get a sanitized sample. Expect a first pass by Thu 5/21 EOD.
- Quantization: we're conservative on core customer-facing chat models but are open to 4-bit for internal recommendation models and some background classification jobs.
- Batching: our current endpoints are synchronous and impact user-perceived latency; if Redwood can preserve sub-300ms p95 with batching for the recommendation flow that would be a big win.

One ask: can you include in the cost sheet an explicit line comparing our current Triton-based costs (rough estimates below) vs projected Redwood costs for the same traffic shape? I'll paste our rough numbers: approx $0.12/token (rounded blended) across models today at our current 2M tokens/day average.

We'll aim to get the traces and a brief note on token split to you by Thu.

- Samir
Samir Patel
Head of ML Platforms | FinTechCorp
samir@fintechcorp.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@redwood.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: inference costs & next steps

Appreciate the quick reply, Samir - good notes. A few follow-ups inline:

- Cost comparison: yes - the attached spreadsheet includes a row-for-row comparison using your estimate of ~$0.12/token (I also included sensitivity levers for batching hit-rates, prefix caching, and quantization levels).
- Quality guardrails for quantization: we'll propose a short A/B eval plan for the first pilot models (control vs 4-bit/8-bit), and we can block traffic to a small % for human review before full rollout.
- Latency with batching: our runtime supports adaptive batching and prefix/KV caching; from experience a well-tuned recommendation flow with high hit-rate often sees token-level cost reductions and maintained end-to-end latency under 300ms p95. We'll produce a conservative and an optimistic projection.

I'll send a calendar invite for the Wed 5/27 10am PT deep-dive - Ben (runtime engineer) will lead that call and bring a short slide deck on quantization + batching tradeoffs. Rachel (CS) will outline rollout/monitoring playbooks.

If anything else comes up, flag it here. Otherwise expecting your sanitized traces by Thu.

Best,
Marissa
